tools.description: Kilo Code is an agent that runs across VS Code, JetBrains and a CLI, offering more than 500 models, bring-your-own-key and local model routing. Its free tier routes requests to free models through the Kilo Gateway with no card required, and the client code is MIT licensed.
tools.pricing_reasoning: MIT-licensed clients that work with your own keys or local models; the free Kilo Auto routing requires no card but the vendor publishes no allowance, so it is treated as open source rather than a generous free tier.
pros: Free routing to free models with no credit card
500+ models plus bring-your-own-key and local options
MIT-licensed editor and CLI clients
cons: The free routing allowance is not published
Gateway and cloud backend code is source-available, not MIT
Teams plan is $15 per user per month
free_tier_limits: The VS Code extension, JetBrains plugin and CLI are MIT-licensed.
The platform plan is free for individuals, and Kilo provides free models for coding tasks through its gateway and partner providers.
Auto Free (`kilo-auto/free`) is listed as the easiest starting route.
No numeric allowance is published for the free routing.
tools.overage: Paid usage comes from your own provider account or the Teams and Enterprise plans; autocomplete through a provider such as Mistral draws on that account’s limits.
tools.setup_notes: Install the extension, plugin or desktop app, then choose Auto Free or connect your own provider account.

faq.question: Is Kilo Code free?
faq.answer: The clients are MIT and the platform plan is free for individuals; free models are offered through Kilo’s gateway without a published allowance.

faq.question: How do I avoid charges?
faq.answer: The vendor’s advice is to choose free models where available and keep autocomplete inside your provider’s free allowance, or disable it.

tools.name: Qwen Code
tools.tagline: Apache-2.0 terminal coding agent optimised for Qwen models, with any provider you supply
tools.description: Qwen Code is an open-source coding agent for the terminal, with optional editor integration, tuned for the Qwen model family. The vendor free OAuth tier ended in April 2026, so it is now free software rather than a free service: you run it against your own API key, OpenRouter, Fireworks or an Alibaba Cloud coding plan.
tools.pricing_reasoning: The Qwen OAuth free tier was discontinued on 15 April 2026, so the tool is free software rather than a free service: it works with your own key, OpenRouter, Fireworks or a paid Alibaba Cloud plan.
pros: Apache-2.0 agent with no vendor lock-in
Accepts OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini-compatible endpoints
Custom provider support covers local servers and proxies
cons: The vendor free tier ended on 15 April 2026
The route it recommends, Alibaba Cloud Coding Plan Pro, is $50/month
Tuned for Qwen models, so other providers need extra setup
free_tier_limits: The CLI is Apache-2.0 and free software, and it works with your own key, OpenRouter, Fireworks or a local model.
The Qwen OAuth free tier was discontinued on 15 April 2026, so there is no vendor-funded free service.
Alibaba Cloud offers subscription plans — a Coding Plan with a weekly quota, or a Token Plan with a monthly credit quota.
tools.overage: There is no free allowance to exhaust: usage is billed by the provider you choose, or by an Alibaba Cloud subscription plan.
tools.setup_notes: Install the CLI, then pick a provider — a Qwen account with a subscription, a standard API key, or a local model through Ollama or vLLM.

faq.question: Is Qwen Code still free to use?
faq.answer: The software is Apache-2.0 and free, but the Qwen OAuth free tier ended on 15 April 2026 — you now supply your own key or subscription.

faq.question: What can I connect it to?
faq.answer: It speaks OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and Qwen APIs, and also runs against third-party providers or local models such as Ollama and vLLM.

tools.name: Mistral Vibe
tools.tagline: Mistral chat assistant and Apache-2.0 coding CLI in one product, formerly Le Chat
tools.description: Vibe is Mistral single product for chat and code: the web and mobile assistant formerly called Le Chat, plus a coding agent in VS Code, JetBrains and the terminal. pros: One product covers chat, web search and terminal coding
The CLI is Apache-2.0 and accepts your own API key
Free plan needs no card and includes 100+ connectors
cons: Free limits are described only as limited, with no numbers
All-day coding in the CLI needs the $14.99/month Pro plan
Rebranded from Le Chat, so older guides point at the old name

tools.setup_notes: Install the CLI, then sign in with a Mistral account or an API key; if the command is not found in a new terminal, run `uv tool update-shell`.

faq.question: What does the free plan include?
faq.answer: Chat, search and image editing, plus limited coding sessions — with limited messages and web searches and no published numbers.

faq.question: How much is the paid plan?
faq.answer: Pro is $14.99/month, subject to fair usage limits and Mistral’s terms.

faq.question: Why can’t I create a Gradio Space?
